senses.gloss: (b. h.) [to be rubbed off, be white,] to be clean, clear (cmp. זָכָה).

units: <cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 1:12">Ex. R. s. 1</cite> <he>ומְנַקֶּה אותם</he> and cleansed them (the new-born); <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 164">Yalk. ib. 164</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 354">Yalk. Ez. 354</cite>; (<cite ref="Sotah 11b">Sot. 11ᵇ</cite> <he>מנקיר</he>).
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 93b:5">B. Kam. 93ᵇ</cite> <he>פשתן ונִיקָּהוּ</he> if he stole flax and cleansed (bleached) it; <cite ref="Tosefta Bava Kamma 10:2">Tosef. ib. X, 2</cite>; a. e.
<cite ref="Yoma 86a:5">Yoma 86ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Exodus 34:7">Ex. XXXIV, 7</cite>) <he>מנקה הוא וכ׳</he> he clears the repentant sinners &c.
Pesik. R. s. 42 כדי לנַקּוֹת את שרה in order to clear Sarah (from suspicion); a. fr.—Part. pass. מְנוּקֶּה, pl. מְנוּקִּין clear, clean, bare.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 36b:9">Snh. 36ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>כשם שב״ד מנ׳ בצדק … מנ׳ מכל מום</he> as the judges must be clear (from suspicion) as to righteousness, so must they be clear of every blemish (of descent).
<cite ref="Gittin 86a:2">Gitt. 86ᵃ</cite> <he>מ׳ מכל מום</he> free from all objectionable qualities; a. e.

<cite ref="Tosefta Sotah 2:3">Tosef. Sot. II, 3</cite> <he>שנ׳ ונקתה נִקְּתָה מכל פורעניות וכ׳</he> (v. ed. Zuck. note) the text says (<cite ref="Numbers 5:28">Num. V, 28</cite>) ‘and she shall be cleared’, she shall be cleared (released) from all the evils which might come upon her deservedly (because she gave rise to suspicion through her conduct).

<cite ref="Numbers 5:28">Ib.</cite> <he>שניקללה ניוולה</he> (Var. <he>שניקל</he>) read: <he>שניקתה בניוולה</he> she is released from further visitation (being sufficiently punished) by her exposure to disgrace. Pesik. R. l. c. <he>היאך … מִתְנַקֵּת</he> by what severe means has Sarah been vindicated!
Kidd. 62ᵃ (ref. to הִנָּקִי, Num. V, 19) הַנְקִי כתיב it may be read hanḳi, clear thy life out of thy body (die, if thou art guilty); v. חָנַק.
